objectives.talk_lola: Lola is outside. Talk to her.
objectives.buy_vinegar: Buy vinegar at the sari-sari store.
objectives.bring_vinegar: Bring the vinegar home to Lola.
objectives.ask_tin: Ask around about Lola's tin box.
objectives.old_places: Old places: the store, the court, the school.
objectives.more: More is coming back. Walk the rest of the barangay.
objectives.tree: There was a tree. Past the plaza.
objectives.bring_tin: Bring the tin box home to Lola.

errands.glue: Bring the glue and nails to Mang Tonyo.
errands.linda: Tell Ma'am Linda about the chairs.
errands.mila: Bring the list to Ate Mila at the carinderia.
errands.berto: Stop by Kuya Berto at the panaderia.

photo.before: Four kids in front of the store, squinting. One is holding a biscuit tin like it matters. You don't remember who took this.
photo.after: Four kids in front of the store. At the bottom of the frame, the long shadow of someone holding a camera, wearing a duster.

letter: It takes so long to be big. Lola says
be home before dark EVERY DAY.
When I am big I will come home
Buy Lola a new tin. I took this one.
lolaLetter: I dug it up the next day. I read it.
I put it back too. I didn't touch
Just come home once in a while.
Even if it's not before dark.
closing: We spent our whole childhood in a hurry to grow up.
It was the dumbest thing we ever wished for.

going.store: Just going to the store. We're missing something in the kitchen.
going.market: Heading to the market before the good vegetables run out.
going.cart: Fishball first. I've been craving it all day.
going.carinderia: I'll eat at Mila's first. I'm starving.
going.bakery: Getting some bread. Probably still warm.
going.bench: Just going to sit for a bit. My feet hurt.
going.court: Going to watch at the court. Someone's still playing.
going.lot: To the empty lot! There are chickens there!
going.creek: Just to the creek. It's cooler there.
going.wake: On my way to your house. Let's walk together.

doing.store: Waiting for Cora. She takes forever with the change.
doing.market: Checking if it's fresh. You can't rush this.
doing.cart: Five more, Manong. The spicy sauce.
doing.carinderia: Adobo today. It's always adobo, but it's good.
doing.bakery: Just the smell fills me up.
doing.bench: Just resting. The breeze is nice here.
doing.court: Look at that kid. Here every day, all alone.
doing.lot: They're so fast! I can't catch them!
doing.hangout: Just chatting. Nothing new, but it's nice.
doing.wake: We're right here. You're not alone.

nena: Oh, is that you? I didn't recognize you. You used to be so skinny.
I'll stop by your house later, okay? I'll bring ginataan.
You kids used to be the loud ones on this street. Now it's just me.
jun: Hey. What's new? I own the pisonet now. Yeah, the one we used to hang out at.
Hardly anyone plays anymore. Everyone has a phone.
You still owe me five pesos. Joking. Not joking.
liza: Hey! When did you get here? Come visit the house, okay?
Have you seen Ma'am Linda? She still asks about you.
Time goes so fast. Feels like yesterday you were crying on the court.
ben: You're the grandchild from the house on the corner, right? You look like your father.
I'm the one who poured the cement on this road. Look, still in one piece.
Don't rush, hijo. Everything is right here.
baby: Ay naku, you're so big now! Are you married yet?
No? Too bad. I have a niece. Very nice.
Fine, fine. Just eat. You're so thin.
rudy: Just got off work. They're building something on the next corner.
Every empty lot here has a buyer now. Shame about the trees.
The old tree? Not yet. Nobody has the nerve.
ising: I know you. You're the kid who always asked what time it was.
I'm not in a hurry anymore. Nothing left to chase.
I used to court your Lola. Don't tell anyone.
bong: Kuya, they say you live in Manila now? Is it true nobody talks to their neighbors there?
I want to leave this place too. Everything is so slow.
jenjen: Kuya, how old are you? ...Wow, you're old.
When I grow up I'm going to be a pilot. Tomorrow, hopefully.
Lola Nena says I have to be home before dark. Every single time.

store: The counter is above your head. You have to reach up and feel for it.
You pour the coins out of the tin. They roll everywhere.
"One ice candy, please. The mango one."
"You're one peso short."   "...Can I owe you?"
A hand comes down through the window with the ice candy anyway.
"When I'm big I'll buy the whole store."
court: The court goes on forever. The ring is higher than the roofs.
"Last shot! Last shot before it gets dark!"
"When I'm big I'll dunk on all of you."
"When I'm big I'm not even coming back here. I'm going to have a car."
Someone laughs. Somebody's lola is already calling.
The tin box sits by the post, where nobody will step on it.
school: The line is long and the sun is already hot. Everyone is singing.
The pole goes all the way up to where the airplanes are.
"Ma'am, how many more years until I'm done?"
Eight. You count it on your fingers and run out of patience first.
chapel: It is still dark. Lola's hand is the only warm thing.
The candles are taller than you. Everyone is whispering the same words.
You fall asleep against her arm before the second song.
"When I'm big, I'm never waking up this early again."
Afterwards there is bibingka, and that is the whole reason you came.
market: Everything is at the height of your eyes: knees, baskets, the tails of fish.
"Hold on to my skirt. Don't you let go."
You let go once, for one second, to look at the chicks dyed pink and green.
The whole market is strangers. Then her voice, saying your name the long way.
"When I'm big, I'll carry the bayong."
bakery: Four in the morning smells like bread.
Ten pesos in your fist, folded so small it's damp.
You eat two on the way home and blame the bag.
"When I'm big I'll eat pandesal until I'm full. Nobody will count."
fountain: The fountain is on. It is on because it is fiesta.
There are banderitas from every roof to every other roof.
Someone's tito is singing. He is not good. Everyone claps.
You and the others throw one-peso coins in and wish for the same thing.
pisonet: One peso. Five minutes. You have four pesos and a plan.
The chair is too high. Half the letters are rubbed off the keyboard.
"Hey, extend me! I'll pay you back tomorrow!"
Somebody's mother appears in the doorway holding one tsinelas.
"When I'm big I'll have my own computer. And nobody will time me."
bench: Your feet don't reach the ground from here.
Lola is picking stones out of the rice. You are supposed to be helping.
The streetlights come on one at a time, the far one first.
"Don't be in a hurry. Time isn't running away from you."
tree: The hole took all afternoon. Your hands are black.
The marble goes in. The teks. The letter, folded eight times.
"Nobody opens it until I'm big. Promise."
You pat the dirt flat and jump on it, to be sure.
creek: The water is up to your chest, and brown, and perfect.

credits.footageBy: kites at dusk, shared by the team

store.how: The coins rolled everywhere. Pick them all up.
store.won: Every last coin, even the one by the step.
store.lost: Some rolled under the store and never came back.

school.how: Sing along: press E as each note reaches the circle.
school.won: You sang every word, loudest in the line. Ma'am gave you a star on your hand.
school.lost: You mumbled the words you didn't know. So did everyone.

chapel.how: Stay awake! Press E to open your eyes.
chapel.won: You made it to the second song. You fell asleep during the third.
chapel.lost: You fell asleep against her arm before the second song.

bakery.how: Catch the hot pandesal in the bag. Move left and right.
bakery.won: Ten, hot, and two more for the walk home.
bakery.lost: Some fell on the floor. The baker put extra in the bag anyway.

fountain.how: E to choose the way, E again to throw. Two coins in the water.
fountain.won: Two coins in. You never said the wish out loud, so it still counts.
fountain.lost: Your coins hit the rim and rolled under the stage. You wished anyway.

pisonet.how: Dodge the blocks until the money runs out. Move left and right.
pisonet.won: All four pesos, and a new high score. Your initials, typed with the three letters that still worked.
pisonet.lost: Game over on the second peso. You watched the others play the rest.

bench.how: What do you say to her?

choices.reply: "Don't be in a hurry. Time isn't running away from you."

choices.say: "Lola, will you still be here when I'm big?"
choices.reply: "Of course. Who else will make you eat?"
She hums. You find another stone, then another.
choices.after: It is the best part of the day and you don't know it yet.

court.how: Press E when the marker is in the gold. Two out of three.
court.won: Two out of three. Nobody believed it, so you said it again all the way home.
court.lost: Nothing went in. Kuya said it was the wind. There was no wind.

market.how: Find Lola (lavender, white hair). Walk into her. E to call her.
market.won: You found her first. She held your hand so hard it hurt, and pretended she had not been scared.
market.lost: She found you. Her voice, saying your name the long way, and then her hand, so hard it hurt.

creek.how: Get to the deep part. When Aling Ising looks up, hide behind a bush or the bench.
creek.won: Past Aling Ising and her washing, into the deep part. She never even turned around.
creek.lost: Aling Ising saw you, all three times. You went in anyway.

lola_intro: @lola: Oh, you're up. Have you eaten?
@lola: There's still fried rice on the table. You always skip breakfast when you come home.
@lola: Anak, go buy some vinegar from Cora first. Just the small one. Tell her to put it on the list.
lola_errand_wait: @lola: Vinegar, anak. From Cora. Just over there, past the court.
lola_thanks: @lola: There. Just put it in the kitchen later.
@lola: One more thing, anak. I can't find my old tin box. The biscuit one, with the dancing ladies on the lid.
@lola: Maybe someone in the neighborhood saw it. Ask around, ha?
@lola: And walk slowly. You walk like someone is chasing you.
lola_waiting: @lola: You haven't found it yet? That's all right, take your time.
wake_arrive: The streetlight in front of the house is already on.
Every door on the street has lent its chairs. They are all here, facing the same way.
@cora: Oh, you're here. Where have you been? We've been looking for you all afternoon.
@tonyo: Leave it. The kid was just out walking.
Nobody says anything else. Somebody puts a cup of coffee in your hands.
door_final: The door is open. It was never locked, and nobody has locked it now.
She is in the sala, where the good chairs used to be.
She looks like she is resting her eyes, the way she did after lunch.
You open the tin again. Under the teks, taped inside the lid, there is a second paper.
door_all: You walked the whole barangay today. Everything was where she said it would be.
cora_first: @cora: Oh! It's you. You've gotten so big. When did you get in?
@cora: Only until Sunday, they said? What a shame. So short.
cora_suka: @cora: Go on. Take it. Don't pay for it.
She wraps the bottle in newspaper more carefully than a bottle of vinegar needs.
cora_favor: @cora: Since you're walking around anyway. Bring this to Mang Tonyo for me.
A tube of glue and a small box of nails.
cora_tin: @cora: Naku. You used to bring that here every afternoon. Rattling. All one-peso coins.
cora_photo: She unpins a photograph from the wall behind the candy jars. The tape has gone yellow.
@cora: It's yours. I don't know who took it. Not me, I was busy counting your coins.
Press Q to look at the photograph.
cora_after: @cora: Ice candy is five pesos now. Everything goes up, right?
@cora: Except the roof. The roof is still the same roof.
tonyo_first: @tonyo: Hot today, no? The kids don't come out here much anymore.
@tonyo: Used to be loud every afternoon.
tonyo_tin: @tonyo: Your Lola's tin? I borrowed it once. For nails. I returned it! Promise.
@tonyo: Last time I saw that thing, you had it. You and that whole noisy gang, running to the court.
@tonyo: You'd play until the streetlights came on. Then all the lolas would start shouting names.
@tonyo: Quiet now. I liked it better loud.
tonyo_delivery: @tonyo: Ah, here it is. Thanks. I've been waiting for this.
@tonyo: I'm fixing up the old chairs. We'll need a lot of them tonight.
@tonyo: Tell Ma'am Linda for me: the school's chairs, I'll pick them up myself. She just needs to handle the key.
tonyo_after: @tonyo: If you see your friends, tell them the ring is still bent. Nobody ever paid me to fix it.
linda_first: @linda: Yes? The office is closed already... Oh. Is that you?
@linda: Grade four. Back row. Always looking at the clock.
linda_tin: @linda: A tin box? Hay. I confiscated that from you once. You cried, so I gave it back.
@linda: Go in, look around. Nobody's here. The flagpole is the same one.
linda_message: @linda: The chairs? Yes, of course. Tell him to pick them up before five.
@linda: And they sent you, of all people. You, of all people. ...All right.
@linda: Drop this off with Mila at the carinderia too. Just a list. For tonight.
linda_after: @linda: They all come back taller and quieter. I never get used to it.
court: The ring is bent a little. The net is gone.
One kid, shooting alone. It used to take ten of you just to get a turn.
baller: He passes you the ball. You miss. He is polite about it.
@baller: Nobody else plays anymore. Everyone's at home.
nena: @nena: Oh, is that you? I didn't recognize you. You used to be so skinny.
@nena: Well, I'm off to the market. Say hi to your Lola for me.
jun: He is already past you. Everyone here walks like they have somewhere to be now.
liza: @liza: Hey! When did you get here? Come visit the house, okay?
She says it the way people say it when they know you won't.
dog: A street dog. It decides you are not interesting, then changes its mind.
cat: Mang Tonyo's cat. It has outlived two bicycles and a karaoke machine.
court_after: The ring is bent a little. The net is gone.
court_bench: Names are scratched into the wood. Yours is there.
flagpole: A flagpole. The rope taps against it when the wind moves.
flagpole_after: The paint has been redone. The rope still taps.
You could almost reach the top if you jumped.
tree: An old tree in an empty lot. The fence has been broken for as long as you can remember.
Something about it. You can't place it yet.
tree_dig: The ground between the roots is soft.
You dig with your hands, like before.
tree_found: Metal. A lid with dancing ladies on it, mostly rust now.
Inside there is a marble, three teks cards stuck together, and a folded paper.
Press R to read the letter.
tree_after: A hole between the roots. Smaller than you'd think.
realize: You take the photograph out again.
The store. The court. Everyone squinting at the sun.
There was one more place. You remember dirt under your nails. You remember a tree.
creek: The creek. Lower than you remember, or the banks got higher.
creek_after: The water goes where it always went.
It doesn't seem to be in a hurry.
kid: @kid: Kuya, do you have load? Let me use your hotspot.
He doesn't look up from the phone.
vendor: @vendor: Fishball, kikiam, kwek-kwek. Just stick and dip.
@vendor: Back then this was all gone by four o'clock. School lets out, instant line.
pisonet: PISONET. P1 = 5 MINS. Under it, a handwritten sign: NO SHOUTING. NO TRASH TALK.
The screens are dark. Through the window: four monitors and one electric fan.
fountain: The fountain hasn't run in years.
Someone still cleans the coins out of it.
fountain_after: No water. A few coins anyway. Someone still wishes here.
pisonet_after: You could pay for all of them now, for as long as you wanted.
lola_bench_after: Your feet reach the ground now. They have for a long time.
chapel: The chapel. The door is open, the way it always is.
chapel_after: The pews have been varnished. They still creak in the same place.
market: Crates of calamansi and string beans. Somebody's radio is on, low.
market_after: You could carry the bayong now. Nobody has asked.
bakery: PANADERIA. The glass case is fogged from the inside.
bakery_after: Pandesal is smaller now. Everyone says so.
carinderia: A bench outside the carinderia, polished by forty years of waiting for rice.
rosa: @rosa: String beans, eggplant, calamansi! Suki, come buy!
@rosa: Oh. You're the kid who got lost here once. Your Lola cried, you know that?
karding: @karding: That's fresh, picked just this morning.
@karding: Hardly anyone shops here anymore. They're all at the mall.
mila: @mila: Eat! There's adobo, there's mung bean stew. It's Friday.
@mila: I still have your father's tab written down. Joking. Eat.
mila_list: @mila: Let me see. ...Pancit, puto, coffee. Lots of coffee.
@mila: We can do that. Tell... never mind, I'll take care of it.
@mila: The bread, that's Berto. Stop by. Tell him it's for your house.
mila_after: @mila: Eat something before you go. You can't have an empty stomach today.
berto_bread: @berto: For your house? Yes, it's set aside.
@berto: I'll bring it over later myself, it's heavy. Don't pay.
@berto: Your Lola's been my suki for thirty years. Four o'clock, every time. Got here before I did.
berto_after: @berto: We'll talk later. I'll be there.
berto: @berto: Pandesal? The fresh batch isn't until four.
@berto: Four in the morning. That hasn't changed. Maybe the only thing that hasn't.
lola_bench: A wooden bench. The right side is more worn than the left.
tires: Mang Tonyo's tires. VULCANIZING is painted on the wall in three different handwritings.
car: A car, parked where you used to draw piko squares in chalk.
home_door: Lola's door. It was never locked, and it still isn't.
